## Summary

Under Section 7(1) of the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, every LLP must have **at least two designated partners**. Both must be individuals, and **at least one must be resident in India**.

Where all partners are body corporates, or the LLP has both individual and body corporate partners, at least two individuals who are partners or nominees of the body corporates must act as designated partners.

Legal currentness is unverified. This is legal information, not legal advice.

## Summary

Under the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (FEMA), a **current account transaction** means a transaction **other than a capital account transaction**.

It includes, among other things:

- Payments connected with foreign trade, ordinary business, services, and short-term banking or credit facilities
- Interest payments on loans and net income from investments
- Remittances for the living expenses of parents, spouse, or children residing abroad
- Expenses relating to foreign travel, education, and medical care of parents, spouse, or children

Under section 5 of FEMA, a person may sell or draw foreign exchange through an authorised person for a current account transaction, subject to restrictions that the Central Government may prescribe in the public interest and in consultation with the Reserve Bank.

The Foreign Exchange Management (Current Account Transactions) Rules, 2000 provide restrictions or approval requirements for certain current account transactions, including transactions listed in their schedules. The supplied rules text is stated to be updated up to 30 June 2023.

## Relevant quotation

> “current account transaction” means a transaction other than a capital account transaction and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing such transaction includes—

> (i) payments due in connection with foreign trade, other current business, services, and short-term banking and credit facilities in the ordinary course of business,

> (ii) payments due as interest on loans and as net income from investments,

> (iii) remittances for living expenses of parents, spouse and children residing abroad, and

> (iv) expenses in connection with foreign travel, education and medical care of parents, spouse and children.

This is legal information, not legal advice. Legal currentness and any subsequent amendments or regulatory changes are unverified.

## Summary

Under section 2(v) of the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (FEMA), a **“person resident in India”** includes:

- An individual who has resided in India for **more than 182 days during the preceding financial year**, subject to the exclusions below.
- Any person or body corporate registered or incorporated in India.
- An office, branch or agency in India owned or controlled by a person resident outside India.
- An office, branch or agency outside India owned or controlled by a person resident in India.

For an individual, the 182-day test does not apply if:

- The person has gone or stays outside India for employment, carrying on a business or vocation, or another purpose indicating an intention to stay outside India for an uncertain period.
- The person has come to or stays in India otherwise than for employment, carrying on a business or vocation, or another purpose indicating an intention to stay in India for an uncertain period.

A person who is not resident in India is treated as a **“person resident outside India.”**

## Relevant quotation

> “person resident in India” means —  
> (i) a person residing in India for more than one hundred and eighty-two days during the course of the preceding financial year, subject to the stated exclusions;  
> (ii) any person or body corporate registered or incorporated in India;  
> (iii) an office, branch or agency in India owned or controlled by a person resident outside India; and  
> (iv) an office, branch or agency outside India owned or controlled by a person resident in India.

Legal currentness has not been independently verified. This is general legal information, not legal advice.
